facts.statement: The genus Portugalosuchus was described by Mateus and colleagues in 2018.
Portugalosuchus lived during the Cenomanian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
Fossils of Portugalosuchus date from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The only known fossils of Portugalosuchus come from the Tentugal Formation in Portugal.
facts.quote: it is known from the Upper Cretaceous Cenomanian Tentugal Formation in Portugal

facts.statement: Portugalosuchus is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodyliform.
facts.quote: Portugalosuchus (meaning "crocodile from Portugal") is an extinct genus of eusuchian crocodyliform

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Portugalosuchus azenhae.
facts.quote: The type species is P. azenhae

facts.statement: Portugalosuchus is classified within the family Gavialidae.
A 2021 study placed Portugalosuchus within Crocodylia as a member of Gavialidae closely related to thoracosaurs like Thoracosaurus.
facts.quote: A 2021 morphological study recovered Portugalosuchus within Crocodylia as a member of Gavialidae closely related to similar "thoracosaurs" (e.g. Thoracosaurus)

facts.statement: Researchers have noted that Portugalosuchus might possibly fall outside of Crocodylia entirely.
facts.quote: while also noting that it might also possibly be outside of Crocodylia completely

facts.statement: A 2022 analysis using morphological and DNA data suggested Portugalosuchus is outside Crocodylia as the sister taxon to Allodaposuchidae.
facts.quote: A 2022 tip dating analysis incorporating both morphological and DNA data placed Portugalosuchus outside of Crocodylia, as the sister taxon of the family Allodaposuchidae

facts.statement: If classified as a basal crocodylian, Portugalosuchus would be the oldest known crocodylian.
facts.quote: if so then it would be the oldest known crocodylian to date

rejected.statement: It remains uncertain whether the group known as "thoracosaurs" were true gavialoids.
rejected.quote: though it is uncertain whether "thoracosaurs" were true gavialoids
